summary: This article explains how elevators use cables, a motor-driven wheel, and a counterweight (or oil and a piston) to move safely up and down, and why they made skyscrapers possible.
introduce: Read the title “How Elevators Work” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a wheel with a rope or cable over it, used to lift heavy things
a heavy weight that balances something on the other side
to make two sides equal so that neither one falls

challengeTerms.def: the force that makes it hard for one surface to slide over another
the grip that lets something pull or move without slipping
a part that slides inside a tube when pushed by pressure

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the elevator is one of the most important inventions in cities? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a counterweight and a safety brake each help an elevator.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review pulley, counterweight, and balance, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses friction, traction, and piston to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
